s: Lenskart has delivered strong revenue growth and improving earnings, but the
valuation already requires sustained execution. Our Underweight view and
INR 560 target are based on 70x FY28 estimated parent EPS of INR 7.94.
Against the dated INR 678.20 reference close, this implies 17.4% downside.
The forecasts and price reference are retained from the 2 November draft; this
We estimate revenue of INR 11,755 crore in FY27 and INR 14,823 crore in
FY28. These estimates assume further operating leverage, lower depreciation
intensity and continued international expansion. At the reference price, the
shares trade at 85.5x FY28 estimated earnings. We regard that as demanding
even with a favourable operating trajectory.
The near-term catalyst is the scheduled 4 November earnings release.

Our FY28 base-case earnings require a parent PAT margin near 9.5%. At 70x
earnings, the market reference price would instead require EPS of INR 9.69,
about 22% above our base estimate. The earnings and multiple assumptions
therefore both matter: stronger execution could close that gap, while a
valuation reset could outweigh growth in absolute profit.

omnichannel retail. Customer acquisition through eye tests
and repeat purchasing can support a long growth runway.
The key investment test is whether stores and
manufacturing translate into returns after rent and
reinvestment. We expect earnings growth, but require
valuation discipline at the selected market reference.

The business combines customer acquisition, sourcing and a growing retail network. We model substantial revenue
and parent-earnings growth through FY29. Store productivity, service quality and cash returns remain the central
tests. Strong business execution alone does not establish an attractive share-price return when expectations are high.
The earnings valuation is 70x FY28 parent EPS of INR 7.94, rounded to INR 560. P/E is used because earnings
include financing and lease-accounting costs. Cash is not added again to earnings already including interest income.
The multiple and forecasts are assumptions, not company guidance.
Risks to Rating and Price Target
Upside risks include stronger international margins, faster customer adoption, successful new products and a
persistent valuation premium. Downside business risks include competition, promotional pressure, store
cannibalisation, currency, acquisition integration, dilution and manufacturing utilisation.
The target is unchanged from the 2 November draft. This correction addresses layout and table completeness, not a market update.
